subject: 4CH1
skill: Derive three isotope mass numbers from proton/neutron counts; calculate an abundance-weighted mean and round to one decimal place.

customQuiz.rationale: Preserve four source marks and three isotope rows. Transfer of the historical result-only concessions is an authored candidate policy, not empirical validation. No two/six-mark adaptation.

requirements: Supply three isotope rows with equal proton number and explicit neutron counts and percentage abundances.
Use genuine Mg24/25/26, Si28/29/30 or S32/33/34 nuclei, but clearly state an enriched sample: these are authored proportions, not claims of natural abundances.
Keep all three positive whole-number percentages summing to100. Require one decimal place. Initial domain excludes exact-tenth results and rounding ties.
evidenceContract: Freeze the original table, private exact numerator and rounded/unrounded results before answers.
Public projection contains only prompt, stimulus and maximumMarks; no seed, solution or calibration fixtures.
Keep the source table out of fresh generation. The source-specific wrong-mass aggregate concession is not a generated-response scoring rule.

constraints: Seed modulo60 selects one of3 nuclear triplets and20 bounded abundance triples. Seed diversity does not imply unlimited item diversity.
All rows in one item represent the same element; mass number equals protons plus neutrons.
Use exact integer weighted numerators and denominator100. Filter zero abundances, exact tenths and half-way rounding ties.
No historical source table, nuclear decay, isotope notation recall or natural-abundance claim.
No live registration or validated mark maximum before independent demand, rendering and response calibration.
relationships: For each isotope A=Z+N; weighted numerator=sum(A_i × percentage_i); relative atomic mass=numerator/100.
Round the exact hundredths result to one decimal place.
The source M2 for a correct numerator subsumes M1; the source result-only concessions are four marks rounded and three marks unrounded.
difficultyControls: Three explicit rows preserve mass-number inference, weighting, normalization and rounding demands.
Element/proportion variation, integer presentation and enriched context need empirical difficulty review.
No claim of learner-calibrated or examiner-approved equivalence.

transformations.conditions: Only the60 reviewed finite inputs; source policy transfer and difficulty are unvalidated.
Different isotope counts, percentage formats, rounding ties and mark maxima require separate review.

solutionProcedure: Add protons and neutrons for each mass number.
Multiply each mass number by its corresponding abundance and sum.

criteria.rule: Derive all three correct mass numbers.
Obtain the correct weighted numerator; this correct M2 subsumes M1.
Correct numerator divided by100 or the exact unrounded mean.
Give the correct one-decimal result using the supplied table.

acceptableAlternatives: Source explicitly awards4 for24.3 alone and3 for24.32 alone. Equivalent generated concessions remain an authored provisional transfer.
Equivalent numerical expressions need full transcription; the bounded marker supports only exact mass lists, numerator, denominator and result.
dependencies: Source wrong masses12,13,14 with working1232/100 and final12.3 score3 as an aggregate concession. Do not invent per-mark allocation.

contradictionRules: Conflicting values, wrong denominators, incorrect numerators, unsupported precision and extra evidence defer; no invented universal penalty.

commonErrors.description: Using the neutron column instead of adding protons and neutrons; source photographed working uses12,13,14 despite nearby prose describing protons/atomic numbers.
Leaving the result unrounded; source scheme distinguishes24.32 from24.3.
